message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how you can create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that is equipped with an NVIDIA RTX A6000‑style GPU (the closest supported GPU is the **NVIDIA Tesla A100**) and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important:**  
> Google Cloud does **not** offer an RTX A6000 GPU. The closest GPU that is currently available in the public catalog is the **NVIDIA Tesla A100** (or the older A100‑PCIe). If you absolutely need an RTX A6000, you would have to bring your own hardware or use a different provider that offers that exact GPU.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Item | How to set it up |
|------|------------------|
| **Google Cloud Project** | Create a project in the Cloud Console or use an existing one. |
| **Billing enabled** | Make sure billing is attached to the project. |
| **API enabled** | Enable the *Compute Engine API* (`https://console.developers.google.com/apis/api/compute.googleapis.com`). |
| **Service account** | Create a service account with the `roles/compute.admin` role (or `roles/editor`). Download its JSON key. |
| **gcloud SDK** | Install the Cloud SDK (`curl https://sdk.cloud.google.com | bash`) and run `gcloud init`. |

---

## 2. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Set variables
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"   # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a100"   # closest to RTX A6000
GPU_COUNT=1
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=200GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM configuration |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU(s) |
| `--image-family` + `--image-project` | Installs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the boot disk |
| `--boot-disk-type` | SSD for better I/O |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional script that runs on first boot (e.g., installs CUDA drivers) |
| `--scopes` | Grants the instance permission to access other GCP services if needed |

---

## 3. Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a custom application), here’s the exact payload you would POST to:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "{INSTANCE_NAME}",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y cuda-drivers"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}`, `{ZONE}`, `{INSTANCE_NAME}`, and `{ACCESS_TOKEN}` with your actual values. The `ACCESS_TOKEN` can be obtained via OAuth 2.0 or by using a service account JWT.

---

## 4. Verifying the Instance

After creation, you can verify that the GPU is attached:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --format="json(accelerators)"
```

You should see something like:

```json
{
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 5. Optional: Installing CUDA & cuDNN

If you need CUDA and cuDNN on the instance, add a startup script (as shown above) or SSH into the VM and run:

```bash
# Update & install prerequisites
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential dkms

# Install NVIDIA driver (already pre‑installed on GPU instances)
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470

# Verify driver
nvidia-smi

# Install CUDA Toolkit (replace version if needed)
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-ubuntu2004.pin
sudo mv cuda-ubuntu2004.pin /etc/apt/preferences.d/cuda-repository-pin-600
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/12.2.0/local_installers/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-525.60.13-1_amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-525.60.13-1_amd64.deb
sudo apt-key add /var/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local/7fa2af80.pub
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y cuda

# Add CUDA to PATH
echo 'export PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.2/bin${PATH:+:${PATH}}' >> ~/.profile
echo 'export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}}' >> ~/.profile
source ~/.profile
```

---

## 6. Clean‑up

When you’re done, delete the instance to avoid incurring charges:

```bash
gcloud compute instances delete "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --quiet
```

---

### TL;DR

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-demo \
  --project=my-gcp-project \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=200GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd
```

That’s all you need to spin up a GPU‑enabled VM on Google Cloud that runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. Happy computing!
